title: The Day a Correction Takes Effect on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
The day from which a correction to a Travel Protection Plans certificate takes effect, for the purpose of apportioning a re-rated difference, is read from the ledger of the vacation package the cover was linked to, one of the Vacation Package Products, and from the certificate's own dates.

Where the linked package's ledger carries a line posted under its routine terms after the certificate was issued and that line was posted before the first day of the journey insured, the day the correction takes effect is the day that line posted.

Where the linked package's ledger carries a line posted under its routine terms after the certificate was issued and that line was posted on or after the first day of the journey insured, the day the correction takes effect is the day the certificate was issued.

Where neither holds, the day the correction takes effect is the first day of the journey insured.

A line the operator raised on account of a price guarantee, or on account of the journey being given up, is not a line posted under the package's routine terms, and the day such a line posted never anchors the apportionment.

## The three anchors

| The latest line posted to the package's ledger under its routine terms | The day the correction takes effect |
| --- | --- |
| Posted after the certificate was issued, and before the first day of the journey insured | The day that line posted |
| Posted after the certificate was issued, and on or after the first day of the journey insured | The day the certificate was issued |
| Not posted after the certificate was issued, or no such line at all | The first day of the journey insured |

## Reading the ledger

Both of the first two cases require a line posted under the package's routine terms to fall after the day the certificate was issued; they are told apart by where that line falls against the first day of the journey insured. A line posted on the first day of the journey itself falls in the second case, because that case takes the line as posted on or after that day.

Lines the operator raised on account of a price guarantee, and lines raised on account of the journey being given up, are set aside before any of this is read: they are not lines posted under the package's routine terms, so neither their existence nor their date bears on the answer.

Hypothetically, a certificate issued on the 3rd of a month for a journey beginning on the 20th: a routine line posted to the package on the 11th anchors the correction to the 11th; a routine line posted on the 24th anchors it to the 3rd, the day of issue; and where the only line posted after the 3rd was raised on account of a price guarantee, the anchor is the 20th, the first day of the journey insured.
